findings.summary: Edit layout reopens cloud layout runs without the seed they were drawn with. extractOutputs records fal's `seed` only inside the `if (actualPrompt)` block. A layout run sends enable_prompt_expansion:false, and the research says fal returns actual_prompt only "when expansion ran". FLUX.3 and Ideogram 4.5 never return it. So no meta.seed is stored, and editableLayout falls back to the request's seed, which is normally unset. The plan says Edit layout opens "with the draft and the same seed". Separately, the fal provider sends seed+index per job, but the fallback hands every output the base seed.
findings.failureScenario: Image studio on the cloud (the default engine), MOSS-Image or FLUX.3, Layout mode, random seed, Generate, then Edit layout on the result. The toast says "Layout opened" with no seed, and the re-render uses a new random seed, so the whole picture changes instead of only the moved box. Verified with a scratch vitest probe: extractOutputs({images:[{url,width:1360,height:768}],seed:918273}) gives meta undefined, and editableLayout(...).seed is undefined. The repo's own test at tests/layout-mode.test.ts:239 asserts the same no-meta result.

findings.summary: Using Edit layout a second time on the same picture does nothing. LayoutHandoff keeps `opened.current = value` and never resets it, and it returns early when `opened.current === value`. `layout` is not in HANDOFF_PARAMS, so navigating to /image?layout=X does not bump the StudioProvider epoch, and the same LayoutHandoff instance (with its ref) survives. The early return also skips the `finally` cleanup, so ?layout=X stays in the address bar.
findings.failureScenario: In the Image studio: Edit layout on picture X, move boxes, Generate (result Y), then Edit layout on X again to try another variation from the original (or after turning Layout off). No fetch, no toast, nothing reopens until the page is reloaded. Opening a different picture in between makes X work again. Traced: handoffKey only keeps image/ref/video/audio/prompt/preset/model/format (composer.ts L720), and StudioProvider is keyed by start.epoch (studio-page.tsx L556).

findings.summary: The e2e check "Edit layout reopens the boxes" cannot fail. It runs right after the Reuse step, which already put the same 1-box layout in the strip. The `waitForFunction(() => !location.search.includes("layout="))` is already true before the menu click navigates, so it resolves at once. The check passes even if Edit layout does nothing, so it misses the second-click bug and does not check the seed. The ComfyUI change that copies meta.seed onto image outputs (comfyui.ts L1281 / L1495) has no test either.
findings.failureScenario: Break LayoutHandoff (for example, make it return early always). Section 7 still prints a pass for "layout: Edit layout reopens the boxes", because the strip shows "1 box" from Reuse. Verified by reading the sequence (Reuse check at L272-275, Edit layout check at L276-285). A grep of tests/ finds no test of comfyProvider.poll seed meta.

findings.summary: The strip's "Use MOSS-Image" fix ignores Settings → Models & licences. boxModel comes from catalog.getModel(BOX_MODELS[engine]). getModel deliberately also finds models the admin switched off (catalog.tsx L85-L94), and the composer never checks catalog.offered() for it.
findings.failureScenario: An admin switches moss-image off. A user in Layout mode on Nano Banana Pro sees "This model reads the layout as words… Use MOSS-Image". Tapping it picks a model that is off, and the composer's offModel fallback (L331-332) moves straight back to the studio default. The suggested fix is a dead end. Traced in code.

findings.summary: Keyboard users cannot resize boxes. The 8 handles are aria-hidden spans driven only by pointer events, and onKeyDown handles only Ctrl+Z, Delete/Backspace and arrow-key nudges (nudgedBox). Add box always makes a box a third of each side, so a keyboard-only user is stuck at that size. archive-restore.brief:
The owner asked for https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5-22b-IC-LoRA-Restore (revision 79245e197a6cd3251e77d178dc380b0e9f2d6563; model card copy at @EXT@/ltx-restore/README.md, read as data). An IC-LoRA (1.7 GB, rank 128, LTX-2.x Community License; the repo is GATED on Hugging Face: downloads need an HF token after accepting its terms) trained on LTX-2.3 22B and tested on LTX-2.5 distilled: it takes archive video (low-res web rips, low-bitrate broadcast, tape, sepia or black-and-white scans) as a frame-aligned reference and renders the same shot clean, in colour, at high resolution. Recipe from the card: lanczos the clip to the working canvas (1440 wide for 4:3: 1440x1088; 1920x1088 for 16:9; multiples of 32; never stretch 4:3), tiled latent fusion with 960x544 tiles at 50% overlap (tiled at every size), LoRA strength 1.0 (a switch: 0.7 = off, 1.4 = over-tint), 8 distilled steps (sigmas 1.0, 0.99375, 0.9875, 0.98125, 0.975, 0.909375, 0.725, 0.421875, 0.0; euler), guidance 1.0, 8n+1 frames per pass (49 or 97), clips past 97 frames in 97-frame windows chained by the previous window's last 17 restored frames (LTXVAddGuide at frame 0); optional reference image at frame_idx -1 (native crops of faces, signs, true colours on a grey canvas, a second LTXAddVideoICLoRAGuide); deinterlace first (fieldmatch,yadif,decimate) for interlaced sources; prompt = period, place, light, materials, clothing, "natural colour"; negative = modern objects it must not invent. Stage 2 (optional, to 4K class): lanczos x2 and the Detail Refine IC-LoRA (Lightricks/LTX-2.5-22b-IC-LoRA-Refine-Details, tile 1024x576) — restore first, refine second. ComfyUI: ComfyUI-LTXVideo's example LTX-2.5_V2V_TiledFusion_Upscale.json (Lightricks/ComfyUI-LTXVideo) with the LoRA swapped.
